messages:
maria: kicking off a replay run on yesterday's prod trace, looking for the KV-cache parity weirdness we saw in canary. will stream logs here.
ryan: thanks — whats the sampling config? last time we accidentally favored short sessions.
maria: sample=0.005, seed=42, stratify_by=session_length, dev-shards=8. command:
```bash
./tools/replay --trace s3://prod-traces/2026-03-16.log --sample 0.005 --seed 42 --stratify session_length --shards 8 --out ./replay-out
```
cheng: quick thought — our anonymizer does `hash(user_id) % 1024` which collides with shard mapping; could be causing shard-skew. :thinking:
sam: oooh that would bias which sessions hit which GPU, and kernel selection heuristics are per-shard. that could change batching behavior and kv warmup patterns.
maria: seeing first signs: replay-bot: INFO 2351009883 starting shard 3
maria: replay-bot: DEBUG kernel_selector: chosen kernel=fastgemm_q4_0 for model=gpt-small on shard=3
ryan: jump in profiling: perf difference between runs ~11% p90 token latency on shard3 vs shard4. kernel selector picks different kernel on otherwise-identical requests.
cheng: can you paste the kernel selection debug for two runs side-by-side? i'm betting RNG order or request ordering changed because of sampling+shard mapping.
maria: pasted excerpts:
```
# run A (seed 42, shard 3)
request_batch_order: [u1,u5,u2,u9]
kernel_choice_scores: [0.78,0.52,0.51,0.49]
selected: fastgemm_q4_0
# run B (seed 42, shard 4)
request_batch_order: [u2,u1,u9,u5]
kernel_choice_scores: [0.57,0.56,0.55,0.54]
selected: int8_conv_fallback
```
sam: ordering flips -> different sequence lengths inside a micro-batch -> different kernel heuristics -> different runtime perf. this is consistent with KV warmup differing too.
ryan: also seeing kv-cache hit rate delta: shard3=0.72, shard4=0.43 across same prefix set. that's huge.
cheng: hypothesis: anonymizer hash -> shard assignment -> stable ordering broken -> micro-batch composition changes. fix options:
- make anonymizer independent of shard (use salted hash that doesn't affect shard id)
- do deterministic global sorting before sharding
- fix kernel selector seed+stable tie-breaker
maria: quick experiment planned: rerun with `--deterministic-ordering` and a mapping sanity check. also try `--anonymizer-salt=const` so user hash -> same bucket across runs.
ryan: small change that fixed a related regression before: enforce `batch.sort_by(prefix_length)` before kernel selection. worth trying.
sam: one more note: we saw a perf regression after the runtime 2.4 change where kernel fallback logic changed float thresholds. maybe combine with ordering fixes.
maria: running two quick replays now (A: deterministic-ordering; B: anonymizer-salt=const). i'll post perf diffs when done.
replay-bot: INFO 2351009930 run-A finished, artifacts at s3://replay-results/2351009876/run-A
replay-bot: INFO 2351009948 run-B finished, artifacts at s3://replay-results/2351009876/run-B
maria: initial numbers: run-A p90 token latency down 9% on problematic shard, kv-hit rate to 0.69. run-B p90 down 7%, kv-hit 0.71.
cheng: nice — both moves in the right direction. suggests anonymizer-shard coupling was the root cause. next steps:
- roll anonymizer salt change into replay pipeline (non-prod first)
- add deterministic-ordering flag to reproducer tests
- add unit test asserting identical kernel selection for same trace+seed across shards
ryan: also add a perf-smoke to CI that runs a tiny replay and checks kv-hit within tolerance.
sam: +1 on CI checks. we should also document the shard->anonymizer interaction in the runbook.
maria: filing follow-up ticket in backlog: RW-1129 "replay: anonymizer->shard decoupling + deterministic ordering + CI smoke" and tagging for eng-runtime.
ryan: thanks all :thumbsup:
maria: moving the artifacts to a retention bucket and closing this thread unless anyone needs more details.
